summary:
Geological Twin is a research and comparative analysis project developed as part of the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It aims to investigate geological similarities between Earth and Mars using scientific data.
Our project compares Gale Crater on Mars with the Göçü Ancient Lake Shoreline in Konya, Türkiye. Using NASA's publicly available satellite imagery, topographic maps, mineralogical data, and scientific research, we examine the geological structures, sedimentary layers, evidence of ancient water, climate changes, and surface characteristics of both regions.
Our approach investigates how geological formations on Earth can help us understand the environmental conditions of ancient Mars. Through comparative mapping and data analysis, we aim to evaluate geological similarities based on scientific evidence.
Identifying safe landing sites and potential base locations for future missions to the Moon and Mars requires a thorough understanding of surface conditions.
Geological Twin aims to contribute to planetary research by using terrestrial analog sites, making scientific data more accessible, and supporting decision-making for future space exploration.
With our slogan, “Two Worlds, One Geological Story,” we explore the geological evidence shared between planets.
details:
Geological Twin is an innovative project developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It aims to investigate geological similarities between Earth and Mars using scientific data and identify suitable terrestrial analog sites for future space missions.

Our project focuses on Gale Crater on Mars and the Göçü Ancient Lake Shoreline in Konya, Türkiye. By using NASA's open-access satellite imagery, topographic data, mineral maps, and scientific studies, we compare the geological structures, sedimentary layers, evidence of ancient water, climate changes, and surface characteristics of both regions.

The project is based on evaluating topography, geology, environmental conditions, and available resources, which are important considerations for NASA's future missions to Mars and the Moon. Accordingly, we will investigate terrain slope, elevation differences, surface roughness, temperature, humidity, mineral composition, water and ice potential, soil characteristics, and the accessibility of natural resources.

Particular attention will be given to water resources, hydrated minerals, surface materials, and potential local construction materials to assess their resource potential for future exploration missions. We will also examine how ground stability, dust formation, extreme temperature variations, and terrain conditions may affect landing safety, robotic vehicle mobility, and the establishment of exploration bases.

Geological Twin plans to use NASA's MOLA, CRISM, HiRISE, and Curiosity datasets, together with information obtained from Earth observation satellites. Python will be used for data analysis, QGIS for geographic mapping, and HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to develop a user-friendly web interface.

The originality of our project lies in investigating the Göçü Ancient Lake Shoreline as a new candidate terrestrial analog site for Gale Crater and evaluating their similarities through measurable scientific parameters rather than visual observations alone.

The proposed comparison system will present significant similarities and differences between the two regions through maps, graphs, and scientific indicators. This approach aims to help researchers identify suitable analog sites, support mission teams in selecting testing environments on Earth, and encourage students to explore planetary science.

Guided by the concept “Two Worlds, One Geological Story,” Geological Twin aims to build a scientific bridge between Earth's geological history, the exploration of Mars, and the future of sustainable space research.
